housing: Torridge is a rural district in north-west Devon, centred on Bideford, with about one in five households renting privately. Bideford and Appledore have steep streets of older terraces and cottages, while Westward Ho! has holiday flats and chalets alongside family homes. The inland villages have cob and stone cottages, farmhouses and barn conversions, many on oil or LPG heating. Rents are among the lowest in the South West.
checkinTips: Coastal homes in Westward Ho!, Appledore and Hartland: check window frames, metal fittings and outside paintwork for salt and wind damage.
Cob and stone cottages: photograph walls for damp, cracks or crumbling render, and note any limewash or breathable paint.
Rural homes off the gas grid: record the oil tank or LPG supply, fuel level, private water supply or septic tank, and boiler service label.
Steep-street terraces in Bideford: photograph steps, handrails, retaining walls and any damp in rear rooms.
Former holiday flats let long term: note furniture and appliances supplied and their condition, room by room.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can contact Torridge District Council's housing regulation team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions.
